title: Co-packaged optics reliability and serviceability
bottleneck: Co-packaged optics places lasers and photonic engines next to hot switch ASICs, exposing them to thermal cycling, vibration, and dust in data centers. Lasers age and fail, but replacing a co-packaged optical engine means servicing or scrapping the whole package, unlike pluggable modules that hot-swap. Reliability data for CPO in harsh field conditions is thin.
why_it_blocks: If CPO can't match pluggable reliability and serviceability, operators won't adopt it despite bandwidth and efficiency gains, and the copper-interconnect energy wall stands. The industry risks a standoff where the needed technology exists but is undeployable.
current_state: CPO products are entering early deployment with major switch vendors, and reliability testing programs are underway. Field-proven multi-year lifetimes at scale are not yet established.
